newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London stable before election.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London stable before election.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were steady in quiet trade on Thursday afternoon, taking their cue from a lacklustre close on Tokyo as investors played safe ahead of the weekend's general election in Japan.
The Nikkei/Ise 50 index was up 0.42 point at 1,462.91 after the Nikkei in Tokyo closed 26.55 points higher at 21,423.74.
"It's very quiet in London but things are looking a little firmer and we could push up tomorrow in anticipation of a good result in the elections," one trader said.
Dealers said the market was buoyed by talk of the LDP party launching a spending package by year-end, if elected.
Surveys show the business-friendly Liberal Democratic Party is likely to win a simple majority in parliament.
"That could give construction and real estate stocks a lift," the dealer said, noting that the relatively strong dollar and a higher opening on Wall Street could boost sentiment.
They noted some bargain hunting in airline JAL, which dropped recently on fears of greater domestic competition.
Other gainers included Bridgestone. Among financial institutions, Bank of Tokyo, Mitsubishi Bank and Sakura Bank were said to be well bid.
